stimulus:
Shards (use any, none, or their collisions as lenses; do not mention them directly):

1. Kintsugi: the break is filled with gold, and the repair becomes the most valued feature.
2. Mycorrhizal tithing: a tree hands sugar to a fungus, and the fungus passes it to a neighbor in shade.
3. Campanology change ringing: bells never repeat a permutation, yet each moves only one place at a time.
4. Salt-marsh tide tables written by a blind ferryman who relies on sound.
5. Medieval commons law: a resource survives because grazing rights are tied to unwritten obligations.
6. Moiré: two regular gratings create a slow pattern neither contains.
7. Sourdough inheritance: a hundred-year-old culture is a community that has been fed, not a single organism.
8. Tidal-lock courtship of two moons that show each other only one face.
9. A cartographer who deliberately draws the unknown regions larger than the known.
10. Pidgin to creole: grammar emerges in children from broken input.

Collisions: lichen / auction / lullaby / fault line / vaccine / abacus / stutter / reef / ledger / eclipse / glue / tremor / loom / quarantine / echo / rust.

Invert one assumption. Ask what would be measured if the noise were the signal, if the failure were the product, or if the observer were part of the instrument.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Prior-stimulus ATAC/CUT&Tag time course with AP-1 degron
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., macrophages or fibroblasts with LPS, TNF, or wounding signals), wash out, and track chromatin accessibility, AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and H3K27ac at 'latent' enhancers for days to weeks. Test necessity by acutely degrading (dTAG/AID) AP-1 factors at different times: before the first stimulus (is it needed to write memory?) versus after it (is it needed to maintain memory?).

ideas.title: Re-stimulation response kinetics as a memory readout
ideas.description: Challenge primed versus naive cells with a second stimulus after varying rest intervals, and measure the transcriptional response (bulk or scRNA-seq, nascent RNA via PRO-seq) for faster, stronger or qualitatively different induction. Compare AP-1 site mutants (CRISPR editing of motifs at specific enhancers) or dominant-negative A-FOS with wild type to show that the primed response depends on AP-1 and to measure the memory half-life.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics with heritability analysis
ideas.description: Use endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and an AP-1 reporter to follow lineages through divisions, quantifying pulse frequency, amplitude and the dynamics of a reporter gene. Treat cell-to-cell variability as signal: test whether sister cells' AP-1 history correlates with each other's re-response beyond what shared lineage alone predicts. Comparing correlation decay over generations to that of shuffled controls estimates mitotic heritability.

ideas.title: Sufficiency test by synthetic AP-1 pulses and optogenetic writing
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 activity with optogenetic or chemogenetic control (e.g., light-gated JUN/FOS, or a stimulus-free dCas9-activator at AP-1 sites), varying pulse duration, frequency and dose in the absence of any natural stimulus. Then measure whether chromatin opening and enhanced re-response persist after AP-1 is turned off, and which pulse patterns are encoded, to separate AP-1 as a writer of memory from a passive reader of other marks.

ideas.title: Cooperating-factor and chromatin-remodeler dependency mapping
ideas.description: Combine CUT&RUN/ChIP-seq, Micro-C or Hi-C and proteomics (BioID) for AP-1 and its partners (BAF/SWI-SNF, pioneer factors, ATF/CEBP/ETS) at memory-bearing enhancers, then perturb the partners with CRISPR screens or inhibitors. Determine whether memory persists via AP-1 occupancy itself, via remodeler-deposited nucleosome changes or histone marks that outlast AP-1, or via self-reinforcing feedback such as AP-1 inducing its own genes (FOS, JUN), by testing which layer is lost first after AP-1 loss.
